transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-29 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~48m
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Ethan Morales (Redwood CSM); Marcus Lee (CPO), Anna Gomez (Legal), Sofia Patel (Head MLOps), Liam O'Connor (Procurement)

--- Summary (auto):
Short run through of MSA/DPA status, SLAs, pricing options. Action items captured at end.

00:00 Jared Kim: hey all, thanks for joining, um, appreciate you making time. quick intro from our side - i'm Jared AE for this account, with priya who's our solutions engineer, and ethan on the onboarding side.
00:10 Marcus Lee: thanks Jared, Marcus here. we'll, we'll jump in - lots on the plate, legal and procurement on the line.
00:16 Anna Gomez: hi all, anna from legal. i saw the MSA, had a few redlines we'll walk through.
00:22 Priya Rao: great, i'll do a quick overview of the SLA and perf stuff and then we can get into the actual redlines.
00:30 Liam O'Connor: from procurement side, main things are pricing tiers, volume discounts, and onboarding timeline.
00:38 Priya Rao: ok cool. quick product note: Redwood Dedicated is our reserved capacity option, gives you predictable throughput. Redwood Private is the VPC / on-prem option for data residency. our hosted api has usage pricing.
00:52 Sofia Patel: just to flag - we have strict regional residency: eu-west and us-east only, and retention rules - clinical data, need 7 years retention and audit logs accessible.
01:05 Anna Gomez: and on DPA we have some required language around subprocessors and breach notification timelines - 48 hours is a hard ask for us.
01:15 Jared Kim: understood. on the breach notif timeline we typically commit to 72 hours in the standard DPA, we can discuss options - need to check with security.
01:25 Ethan Morales: quick note, we can provide SOC 2 and ISO artifacts; also we have KMS integrations for customer-managed keys in Private.
01:35 Marcus Lee: ok, so high level, we want to pilot with hosted first for speed, but evaluate Dedicated for predictable latency. pricing wise we need a committed arrangement for the pilot and an option to convert to dedicated reserved capacity.
01:50 Priya Rao: fair. for latency numbers - for 8k contexts our median is ~80-120ms per token on our optimized runtime on A100 style infra, p95 around 300ms depending on batch and prompt. for 16k contexts these numbers shift, p95 can be 450-700ms on normal configs - we'll run specific with your prompt set.
02:10 Sofia Patel: those numbers sound ok as long as we can get the p99 visibility and a runbook if there are regressions.
02:18 Priya Rao: yes, we produce per-route dashboards in Redwood Console and you can get token-level breakdowns, p95/p99 tracing. we also support KV cache/prefix caching to reduce cost and latency for repeated interactions.
02:32 Anna Gomez: back to the DPA, subprocessors - we need a list and a clause that we can audit them annually. is that possible?
02:40 Jared Kim: we have a subprocessors list in the security pack; we can include audit windows. i need to confirm the annual audit verbiage though - i'll take that back.
02:50 Liam O'Connor: on pricing can you share an estimate for pilot (100K tokens/day) for hosted, and a 3-month committed reserved block pricing for Dedicated?
03:00 Priya Rao: yes, we'll share a pricing deck. host vs dedicated cost delta depends on requests/sec and burst patterns; dedicated becomes cost-effective if you have sustained peak. we'll model both with your traffic.
03:12 Marcus Lee: procurement will need contract lead time, typically 4-6 weeks for review. legal wants the MSA redlines in advance.
03:20 Anna Gomez: we did preliminary redlines - main items: 1) DPA breach notif 48h, 2) data residency clause to lock to eu-west/us-east, 3) retention 7 years for clinical data, 4) liability caps - need to discuss commercial exposure.
03:36 Jared Kim: liability caps - our standard is a multiple of fees - we can discuss higher caps for enterprise. we'll escalate to legal ops and get a response in the redline.
03:46 Priya Rao: technical ask - Sofia, can you share a small sample of your typical prompts and traffic distribution? we'll run benchmarks with those.
03:54 Sofia Patel: yes, can do - a sanitized sample. we need PII removed, but it's mostly clinical Q&A and summarization flows.
04:02 Priya Rao: perfect. we'll run them on the 8k and 16k variants, and include both hosted and dedicated configs. should show latency, token costs, and expected throughput.
04:14 Marcus Lee: how about SLAs - what's typical? uptime, and latency SLOs?
04:20 Priya Rao: uptime: we publish a 99.9% SLA for Dedicated, hosted has a 99.5% public SLA. for latency we don't typically do a hard p99 guarantee on hosted, but for Dedicated we can include latency targets (p95/p99) as part of an SLA appendix for enterprise contracts. we'll need to agree on the workload profile for those targets.
04:40 Liam O'Connor: and credits for SLA misses?
04:42 Jared Kim: yes credits are standard - we'll include credit calc in the SLA appendix - typically pro rata credits per minute of downtime and additional negotiated credits for latency misses if included.
04:52 Anna Gomez: is there an incident escalation path? we need an on-call contact for production incidents and a runbook.
04:58 Ethan Morales: yes, we'll provide a runbook and 24/7 on-call for Dedicated with SRE escalation, and priority support for pilot customers.
05:08 Sofia Patel: regarding KMS - we want customer-managed keys for encryption at rest in Private; is that available for Dedicated or only Private?
05:16 Priya Rao: currently customer-managed KMS is available in Private and in Dedicated on select tiers - we can check eligibility. Hosted currently supports server-side encryption with provider-managed keys, but we can offer Bring Your Own Key in Dedicated/Private.
05:30 Marcus Lee: timeline - we want a pilot in october, 4 weeks, then decision by end of november. is that feasible from your side?
05:38 Jared Kim: yes that timeline is doable. pilot kickoff early october, benchmarks this week after sample prompts, then MSA/DPA redlines early october, onboarding plan by oct 7.
05:48 Liam O'Connor: procurement will need pricing and SOW to start purchase order conversation.
05:54 Jared Kim: we'll deliver pricing and a template SOW.
06:00 Anna Gomez: other legal item - data subprocessor flowdown, can you confirm subprocessors will be flowdowned?
06:06 Jared Kim: yes, we typically flow down key obligations; i'll have legal confirm specifics.
06:10 Priya Rao: technical deep-dive - when should we schedule? would week of oct 4 work? we can bring infra and perf engineers.
06:18 Sofia Patel: yes week of oct 4 works. prefer oct 6 or 7.
06:22 Priya Rao: noted - we'll propose slots.
06:26 Marcus Lee: ok, any competitive traps? our vendor spreadsheet has Anthropic and OpenAI as options - curious what differentiates you on cost & control.
06:36 Jared Kim: main differentiator is serving controls and cost levers - batching, KV cache, quantization profiles, and predictable Dedicated capacity. we also provide observability per-route which helps tie regressions to deploys.
06:50 Sofia Patel: you mentioned prefix caching - does that persist across sessions? we need session continuity for our assistants.
06:56 Priya Rao: yes, KV/prefix caching can be configured; cache policies can be per-customer or per-route, with explicit TTLs.
07:06 Liam O'Connor: are there any non-standard SLAs we should expect for pilot?
07:10 Jared Kim: pilot will have priority support but not full enterprise SLA unless you convert to Dedicated and sign the SLA appendix - but we can negotiate some pilot guarantees in the SOW.
07:22 Anna Gomez: on breach notif again - 48h is our ask; if you can do 72h is that a deal breaker?
07:30 Marcus Lee: for us 48h is strongly preferred; some exceptions maybe ok for forensic delays.
07:36 Jared Kim: understood. i'll circle back with security and legal, and mark this as a key ask in our response.
07:44 Priya Rao: action items recap coming up - we'll put everything in the notes.
07:48 Ethan Morales: onboarding plan - we'll do a 4-week pilot: week 0 (kickoff + access), week 1 (benchmarks + observability dashboards), week 2 (integration + caching), week 3 (pilot run + eval).
08:02 Sofia Patel: sounds good. one more question - egress logging and audit trail retention, can that be exported to our S3?
08:10 Priya Rao: yes, audit logs can be exported; for Private/Dedicated we can ship logs to your S3 with lifecycle rules. hosted can also forward logs to customer destinations with limited retention options.
08:22 Liam O'Connor: ok, procurement comment - we'll need the quote and PO-ready SOW to start internal approvals.
08:28 Jared Kim: we'll put together the quote and SOW and target delivery by 2026-10-06.
08:33 Anna Gomez: great. any outstanding blockers?
08:36 Sofia Patel: we need a sanitized prompt sample and confirmation of regions - we'll send sample by 2026-10-01.
08:42 Priya Rao: perfect. we'll queue benchmarks once sample arrives.
08:46 Jared Kim: to close, next steps recap: redlined MSA/DPA, benchmarks, SLA appendix, pricing/SOW, schedule deep-dive week of oct 4.
08:58 Marcus Lee: thanks everyone - we'll review and get back with legal redlines.
09:03 Anna Gomez: thanks, bye.
09:05 Jared Kim: thanks all, bye.

--- End transcript

Notes: occasional transcription errors present (product names, timings). References to "KV cache" and "prefix caching" appear; customers asked for KMS B-Y-O keys and 48h breach notification. Agreed pilot timeline and deliverables.
